text:
alex_support: FYI — Customer ACME (prod) reports p99 for /v1/generate ~350-450ms from US-WEST since ~09:05 PST. Support traces show tail latency, tagging eng-sre.
elaine: Thanks. Can you paste a trace id and a sample curl from their client region?
alex_support: trace: trc_20260317_09_08_112233, sample curl from their probe:
```bash
curl -w '@curl-format.txt' -o /dev/null -s 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate' -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
# output: time_namelookup: 0.010, time_connect: 0.020, time_starttransfer: 0.420, time_total: 0.423
```
marco: Console metrics show p95 ~95ms, p99 jumped to 380ms around 09:03 and is sustained. Here's the per-pop heatmap — US-WEST pop shows a big tail.
jin_netops: Running traceroute from probe in us-west -> our ingress IP shows an extra hop through AS65055 (transit partner) around hop 5 that wasn't there yesterday. traceroute snippet:
```
traceroute to 34.201.1.2 (34.201.1.2), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.10.1.1 (10.10.1.1)  0.6 ms  0.6 ms  0.6 ms
 2  198.51.100.1 (198.51.100.1)  2.1 ms  2.0 ms  2.1 ms
 3  * * *
 4  203.0.113.7 (203.0.113.7)  85.9 ms  86.1 ms  86.0 ms  <-- big jump
 5  192.0.2.12 (192.0.2.12)  87.0 ms  87.3 ms  87.2 ms (AS65055)
 6  34.201.1.2 (34.201.1.2)  88.0 ms  89.1 ms  88.6 ms
```
jin_netops: MTR from same probe shows latency spike starting at hop 4 -> consistent with a new detour.
ingress-ops-bot: route-control: GSLB weight change applied by netops@09:02:14 — adjusted weight(us-west)=0.6 -> 0.3 for lb-group gamma, reason: traffic shift test.
elaine: That GSLB change might have rebalanced traffic to a different upstream peer with worse AS path. Can we confirm BGP ads or peering changes around 09:02?
jin_netops: Opening bgp dump now. I see new learned path to 34.201.0.0/16 via partner AS65055 at 09:02:19, with community 65535:100 attached.
marco: Customer trace correlation: their internal spans show egress->ingress latency adds ~70-90ms on tail. Application server latencies unchanged. Looks network.
dl_oncall: Mitigation idea: temporarily pin ACME traffic to alternate us-west PoP that keeps direct peering (weight=0.9) while we investigate. We can also add a short-lived static route for their IP blocks.
elaine: Agreed. Marco, can you apply a per-customer routing policy to pin to us-west-1b PoP? Provide the API call.
marco: Doing it now. API call:
```bash
curl -X POST https://control.redwood.example/internal/routing/policies -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"policy_name":"pin-acme-usw-1b-171612","match":{"customer":"ACME","src_region":"us-west"},"action":{"preferred_pop":"us-west-1b","ttl":600}}'
```
marco: Policy applied at 09:12:06. Observing immediate effect on p99 for ACME: lowered from ~380ms -> ~95ms within 30s.
alex_support: Customer confirms improved performance in their synthetic tests — thanks.
jin_netops: I'll open a ticket with partner AS65055: they altered route advertisement/peering path. Adding BGP dumps and timestamps.
ingress-ops-bot: alert: routing policy change recorded by marco@09:12:06 (audit-id rpol_1716123456)
elaine: Good mitigation. Next steps: 1) keep pin for 1 hour while partner ticket progresses, 2) revert the GSLB experiment and coordinate with netops for safer rollout window, 3) add a regression check to our GSLB CI to detect AS path detours that add >30ms.
dl_oncall: Also add a short-term monitoring alert to flag sudden new AS hops on customer-critical flows.
marco: I'll roll back the global GSLB weight change now (netops-approved) and note the incident in the change ticket.
marco: rollback command:
```bash
# rollback weight
curl -X POST https://control.redwood.example/internal/gslb/weights/rollback -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN>' -d '{"change_id":"gslb_ch_20260317_090214"}'
```
marco: Rollback confirmed at 09:18:44, global metrics starting to stabilize.
jin_netops: Ticket created with partner: TP-9823. Attaching traceroutes and BGP dumps.
elaine: Can someone add this to postmortem queue? Include timeline, mitigation, and CL (config) that caused it. Also schedule a follow-up with netops & partner in 24h.
dl_oncall: Done — created incident tracker INC-2026-03-GSLB-HOP. Assigning owners: jin_netops (root cause lead), marco (mitigation), elaine (postmortem/changes).
alex_support: Customer update posted. They want a short RCA once partner responds.
marco: Quick notes for RCA: root cause likely GSLB weight experiment that shifted proportion of traffic to a PoP whose egress path to some ISPs routes via partner AS65055 causing +70-90ms hop. Mitigation: policy pin, rollback weights, partner coordination.
elaine: Add runbook entry: before changing GSLB weights >10% for a pop, run path-diff probe against a list of major customer prefixes and alert on new AS hops or >25ms increase.
jin_netops: I'll extend our BGP collection to capture before/after for GSLB changes going forward.
marco: :thumbsup:
elaine: Closing thread for active mitigation — monitoring for next hour, will update postmortem link in INC-2026-03-GSLB-HOP.
alex_support: Thanks team :heart:
